title: Physical and Chemical Change
description: Physical changes alter shape or state but not composition. Chemical changes create new substances with different properties. Evidence includes colour change, gas production, heat, or light.

exercises.question: Which is the BEST evidence that a chemical change has occurred?
choices: a new substance with different properties was produced
exercises.exp: Chemical changes produce new substances — shown by new colour, smell, gas bubbles, heat, light, or precipitate.

exercises.question: Dissolving sugar in water is a ___ change.
exercises.exp: Dissolving is physical — sugar molecules spread through water but no new substance forms. Evaporate the water and the sugar returns!

exercises.question: Cooking an egg is a ___ change.
exercises.exp: Cooking an egg changes its protein structure permanently — you cannot uncook an egg! That is chemical change.

exercises.question: Which PAIR are both physical changes?
choices: fireworks exploding and leaves changing colour
exercises.exp: Folding paper (shape change) and melting wax (solid to liquid) are both reversible physical changes.

exercises.question: Which PAIR are both chemical changes?
exercises.exp: Rusting (iron + oxygen → iron oxide) and burning (fuel + oxygen → ash/smoke) both create new substances.

exercises.question: Wood burning produces ash, smoke, and heat. Can this change be REVERSED?
choices: no — chemical changes are generally irreversible
exercises.exp: Chemical changes are generally permanent — you cannot turn ash and smoke back into the original wood.

exercises.question: A fizzing tablet dropped in water produces bubbles. This is a ___.
choices: chemical change — a gas is being produced
exercises.exp: Gas production (bubbles) is a sign of chemical change — a new substance (carbon dioxide gas) is being made!

exercises.question: Ice cream left in the sun melts. This is a ___ change.
choices: chemical — it cannot be frozen again
physical — it is still ice cream, just liquid
exercises.exp: Melted ice cream is still ice cream — just in liquid form. Refreeze it and it is (nearly) back to solid!

exercises.question: What happens to ATOMS during a physical change?
choices: they are rearranged into new molecules
they stay in the same chemical combinations — only arrangement changes
exercises.exp: Physical changes do not alter the chemical bonds — atoms stay in the same molecules, just arranged differently.

exercises.question: Photosynthesis in plants (making sugar from CO₂ and water) is a ___.
exercises.exp: Photosynthesis creates glucose (sugar) — a brand-new substance from CO₂ and water. Definitely chemical!

exercises.question: An iron nail left outside turns reddish-brown. This shows ___.
choices: a physical change due to temperature
a chemical change — iron reacted with oxygen and water to form rust
a biological change caused by bacteria
exercises.exp: Rust (iron oxide) is a new substance formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water — a chemical change!

exercises.question: Which observation does NOT indicate a chemical change?
choices: an object being cut into smaller pieces
exercises.exp: Cutting only changes shape — no new substance forms. New colour, smell, or bubbles suggest chemical change.

exercises.question: Mixing BAKING SODA and VINEGAR produces bubbles and a new substance. This is ___.
choices: physical — the substances are just mixing
chemical — gas (CO₂) is produced and the substances are permanently changed
physical — both substances can be recovered easily
exercises.exp: Baking soda + vinegar react to form carbon dioxide gas, water, and sodium acetate — new substances! Definite chemical change.

exercises.question: Crumpling a piece of ALUMINIUM FOIL is a ___ change.
exercises.exp: Crumpling changes shape but not chemical composition — the foil is still aluminium. Physical change!

exercises.question: Bread rising in the oven involves YEAST reacting to produce CO₂ gas. This is ___.
choices: a physical change — bread just puffs up
a chemical change — yeast reacts with sugars producing gas and new substances
exercises.exp: Yeast undergoes fermentation — a chemical reaction producing CO₂ gas that makes dough rise. New substances are formed!

exercises.question: RUSTING is a chemical change because ___.
choices: iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a completely new substance: iron oxide (rust)
rust can easily be turned back into iron
exercises.exp: Rust (Fe₂O₃) is a brand-new compound — iron + oxygen + water form something entirely different. Chemical change!

exercises.question: A physical change is generally REVERSIBLE. Which example is REVERSIBLE?
exercises.exp: Melted butter can be cooled back to solid — it is still butter (just different state). Burning and baking are irreversible chemical changes.

exercises.question: During a CHEMICAL change, the MASS of the system ___.
choices: is conserved — the total mass stays the same
exercises.exp: Conservation of mass: atoms are rearranged, not destroyed. The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products!

exercises.question: Hydrogen PEROXIDE (H₂O₂) slowly breaks down into water and oxygen. This is ___.
choices: chemical — a new substance (oxygen gas) is produced
physical — the water could be turned back into H₂O₂
exercises.exp: H₂O₂ → H₂O + O₂. New substances form — this is a chemical change (decomposition reaction).

exercises.question: TEARING a piece of paper is a ___ change.
choices: chemical — paper becomes a new substance
physical — paper is still paper, just smaller pieces
exercises.exp: Torn paper is still paper — same chemical composition, just different shape and size. Irreversibility does not always mean chemical change.

exercises.question: Milk left out SOURS over time. This is ___.
choices: chemical — bacteria produce new compounds changing colour, smell, and taste
physical — you can make it sweet again easily
exercises.exp: Bacteria ferment lactose in milk, producing lactic acid — a new substance. The smell, taste, and composition all change. Chemical!

exercises.question: Which change can you REVERSE by cooling?
exercises.exp: Melted wax cools back into solid wax — same substance, reversible physical change. Burning, rusting, and baking all produce new substances.

exercises.question: FIREWORKS produce light, sound, and new gases. This is ___.
choices: a physical change — they just make light
a chemical change — new substances are produced in the explosion
exercises.exp: Fireworks undergo rapid chemical reactions — chemicals react to produce entirely new substances (gases, ash) along with light, heat, and sound.

exercises.question: In a PHYSICAL change, which is always preserved?
choices: the chemical identity (composition) of the substance
exercises.exp: Physical changes may alter shape, size, or state — but the chemical composition NEVER changes. It is still the same substance!

exercises.question: PHOTOSYNTHESIS takes CO₂ and H₂O and produces glucose and oxygen. Is this physical or chemical?
choices: physical — the molecules just rearrange temporarily
chemical — completely new substances (glucose, oxygen) are produced from different starting materials
physical — you can easily convert glucose back to CO₂
exercises.exp: Photosynthesis rearranges atoms into brand-new molecules (glucose = C₆H₁₂O₆). Whenever new substances form, it is a chemical change!

exercises.question: DISSOLVING salt in water — can the salt be recovered?
choices: yes — evaporate the water and the salt crystals return
no — it became a new substance
yes — but only by a chemical reaction
exercises.exp: Dissolving is physical — no new substance forms. Evaporate the water and you get your salt back! The salt was just spread through the water.

exercises.question: A CANDLE burns. The wax melts (physical) AND reacts with oxygen to produce CO₂ and H₂O (chemical). A burning candle shows ___.
choices: BOTH physical AND chemical changes happening together
exercises.exp: Wax melting = physical change. Wax reacting with oxygen = chemical change. Both happen simultaneously when a candle burns!

exercises.question: SOAP making: fat + lye (sodium hydroxide) → soap + glycerol. This is ___.
choices: physical — fats and lye are just mixed
chemical — soap and glycerol are completely new substances from fats and lye
exercises.exp: Soap making (saponification) is a classic chemical reaction — fat molecules are broken apart and rebuilt into soap molecules and glycerol.

exercises.question: Two clear liquids are mixed. The mixture turns BRIGHT ORANGE and gets warm. What type of change occurred?
choices: physical — they just changed colour by mixing
chemical — new colour AND heat produced are signs of a chemical reaction
exercises.exp: New colour + heat production = strong evidence of chemical change. A new orange substance with different properties was likely formed.

exercises.question: DIGESTION in your body — food is broken down into simpler molecules your body can use. This is ___.
choices: physical — food is just crushed smaller
chemical — enzymes break chemical bonds, creating new, smaller molecules
physical — you can reassemble food from digested pieces
exercises.exp: Digestion is chemical — enzymes catalyse reactions that break large molecules (proteins, carbs) into small molecules (amino acids, glucose). New substances!

exercises.question: Which is the BEST clue that a CHEMICAL change (not physical) has occurred?
choices: a new substance with different properties was produced
the object changed colour only due to light
exercises.exp: The most reliable indicator of chemical change is production of a new substance with different properties — new smell, gas, precipitate, or light production.

exercises.question: CONSERVATION OF MATTER states that in any chemical change, ___.
choices: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products — atoms are rearranged, not destroyed
exercises.exp: Atoms are rearranged in chemical reactions, never created or destroyed. Input mass always equals output mass — matter is conserved!

exercises.question: Which correctly pairs a change with its TYPE?
exercises.exp: Cutting hair only changes shape/size — it is physical. Rusting and burning produce new substances — chemical. Dissolving sugar is physical (sugar is still there).

exercises.question: ELECTROLYSIS is splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen gas using electricity. This is a ___.
choices: physical change — the water just changes shape
chemical change — water (H₂O) is decomposed into different substances (H₂ and O₂)
exercises.exp: Electrolysis breaks chemical bonds in water, producing completely different gases (H₂ and O₂). A new substance = chemical change!

exercises.question: Why does a banana turn BROWN after being peeled?
choices: it absorbs water from the air
enzymes in the banana react with oxygen in the air — a chemical change called oxidation
it freezes in contact with air
it loses water through evaporation only
exercises.exp: Enzymatic browning: enzymes in banana cells react with O₂, producing brown melanin compounds — a chemical change. Lemon juice (acidic) can slow this reaction.

exercises.question: PHOTOSYNTHESIS is a chemical change because ___.
choices: it only changes the colour of leaves
CO₂ and water (reactants) are converted into glucose and O₂ (new substances with different properties)
it is reversible by removing light
exercises.exp: Photosynthesis produces glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and oxygen from CO₂ and water — entirely new substances with different properties. Definitely chemical!

exercises.question: What is an EXOTHERMIC chemical reaction?
choices: one that absorbs heat from the surroundings
one that releases heat (and sometimes light) to the surroundings
one that requires very low temperatures to proceed
one that only happens in labs
exercises.exp: Exothermic reactions release energy as heat/light. Burning, hand warmers, and rusting all release heat — they make surroundings warmer!

exercises.question: What is an ENDOTHERMIC chemical reaction?
choices: one that absorbs heat energy FROM the surroundings, making them feel cooler
exercises.exp: Endothermic reactions absorb heat from surroundings — making them feel colder. Cold packs in first aid kits use endothermic reactions!

exercises.question: CORROSION of metals is a chemical change. Which BEST prevents iron from rusting?
choices: covering with an insulating paint or a protective metal coating (like zinc — galvanizing)
exercises.exp: Rust requires iron, oxygen, and water. A protective coating (paint, zinc, or oil) prevents O₂ and water from reaching the iron surface — blocking corrosion!

exercises.question: In the reaction: magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide, the REACTANTS are ___.
choices: magnesium AND oxygen — the starting materials that react
exercises.exp: Reactants are starting materials (left of arrow): magnesium and oxygen. Products are what forms (right of arrow): magnesium oxide — a new white powder.

exercises.question: CATALYST chemicals SPEED UP a reaction without being consumed. Which describes a catalyst?
choices: it provides fuel for the reaction
it lowers the activation energy needed, allowing the reaction to proceed faster — the catalyst is unchanged at the end
exercises.exp: Catalysts lower activation energy without being used up. Enzymes (biological catalysts) speed up reactions in our bodies. Industrial catalysts save enormous energy!

exercises.question: You mix baking soda (NaHCO₃) and vinegar (acetic acid). Bubbles form and the container gets slightly cold. This reaction is ___.
choices: chemical and endothermic — new substances form and heat is absorbed
exercises.exp: New substances form (CO₂ gas, water, sodium acetate) = chemical. The container cools = endothermic. Classic endothermic chemical reaction!

exercises.question: Which represents the CORRECT balanced equation for burning methane (natural gas)?
exercises.exp: Methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. The balanced equation CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O conserves atoms on both sides — law of conservation of mass!

exercises.question: ACID-BASE reactions produce salt and water. When hydrochloric acid (HCl) reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH), the products are ___.
exercises.exp: Neutralisation: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Acid + base = salt + water. The NaCl formed is ordinary table salt! Classic neutralisation reaction.

exercises.question: Why do INDICATORS like litmus paper change colour with acids and bases?
choices: they absorb light differently in different temperatures
their molecular structure changes chemically in the presence of H⁺ (acid) or OH⁻ (base) ions, altering which light wavelengths they absorb
exercises.exp: Indicator molecules change structure (chemically) in different pH environments — absorbing different wavelengths of light, producing visible colour changes!

exercises.question: FERMENTATION is a chemical change. Yeast converts sugar into alcohol and CO₂. This is used in ___.
choices: baking bread (CO₂ makes dough rise) and brewing
exercises.exp: Yeast fermentation: sugar → alcohol + CO₂. Bakers use CO₂ to make bread rise; brewers use the alcohol. Ancient humans discovered this chemical change!

exercises.question: The LAW OF CONSERVATION OF MASS means if you burn 12 g of wood to produce 2 g ash and various gases, the gases weigh ___.
choices: 10 g in total — 12 g ash + gases = 12 g total starting mass
exercises.exp: 12 g wood → 2 g ash + gas. Gases must weigh 12 − 2 = 10 g. Total mass of products (2 + 10 = 12 g) = mass of reactants (12 g wood). Conserved!

exercises.question: POLYMERISATION is a chemical reaction that joins small monomer molecules into long chains. This creates ___.
choices: polymers like plastic (polyethylene) and natural polymers like starch
exercises.exp: Polymerisation links thousands of small molecules (monomers) into long chains (polymers). Polyethylene = joined ethylene monomers. Starch = joined glucose monomers!

exercises.question: A PRECIPITATE forms when two solutions are mixed and an INSOLUBLE solid appears. This is evidence of ___.
choices: a chemical change — new insoluble substance produced that neither solution contained before
exercises.exp: Precipitation is a chemical change — new bonds form between ions from different solutions, creating an insoluble solid (precipitate) that settles out!

exercises.question: Which factors can SPEED UP a chemical reaction?
choices: decreasing temperature and using smaller pieces
increasing temperature, increasing concentration, using smaller particle sizes, and adding catalysts
exercises.exp: More temperature = more energy. Higher concentration = more particles colliding. Smaller particles = more surface area. Catalyst = lower activation energy. All speed up reactions!
